svg.title: Milliseconds of wall clock per 1,000 generated tokens
svg.desc: Each bar is one real 2 to 4-hour run (two runs averaged where we had two), split from its SGLang server log. How it's measured: SGLang logs a decode line every 40 steps. Intervals with no prompt read give the pure step time at that lane count. Time beyond that in other intervals is prompt reading, shared out per read by a cost model (per read, per new token, per cached token). Idle lanes are decode time with fewer games running than the server allows. Our offline evaluation has 25 to 75 games, so lanes empty out as games get won; Kaggle's 110 games keep them fuller.

g.aria-label: Milliseconds of wall clock per 1,000 generated tokens
Each bar is one real 2 to 4-hour run (two runs averaged where we had two), split from its SGLang server log.
Overhead: fixed cost per read, stalls
1 Oct · Daniel Franzen's notebook, as published
SGLang fork, MTP drafting, 10 games, 8-bit history cache
3 Oct · + host-RAM cache tier, tuned drafter
parked games keep their history; accepted tokens 2.69 → 2.89
12 games; fused kernels; image hashing moved off the scheduler
11 Oct · + 32 games, a third of the experts cut
4-bit history cache, big-batch kernels, lost-history fix
Mamba 180 slots, 140k window, 24 GB RAM tier
per-game verify depth, 4 draft steps, 3 guaranteed experts, 52k keep
splice, Lean turns, vocab trim; 75-game offline evaluation
